sections.html:
• Origin: Venezuela
  • Maturity is usually reached at a length of 20-25 cm

The Orinoco peacock bass, Cichla orinocensis, is a predatory cichlid from the Orinoco basin in Venezuela and Colombia and the Rio Negro in Brazil. One of the smaller peacock bass, it still grows to around 60 cm and needs a tank of at least 244 x 91 x 91 cm as an adult. It is territorial and moderately aggressive and will eat any tankmate small enough to be considered food.
Native to the Rio Orinoco basin in Venezuela and Colombia, and the Rio Negro in Brazil.
Found in varying habitats in the Amazon basin.

Standard length: 60 cm SL.

One of the smaller Peacock Bass, however a large tank is still required. Ultimately, this fish will require a tank of at least 244 x 91 x 91 cm (l x h x w) for an adult fish. Smaller aquaria can be used for younger specimens but realistically you should not acquire this fish if you cannot house it long term.

This species requires a lot of swimming space, so it is a good idea to furnish the tank fairly sparsely. Large pieces of bogwood and robust plants are recommended. These are large messy fish and require filtration that is up to the job. External or sump filtration should be considered.

Youngsters can be fed with white mosquito larvae and bloodworm; however, feeder fish are ideal. From a size of about 10 cm on, the young Cichla can be fed with frozen smelt as the basic food. Smelt can be used even for the largest specimens.
Piscivorous in nature. The diet should consist of meaty foods such as prawn, mussel, lancefish, whitebait and other white fish.

Territorial and moderately aggressive. Can be kept in species groups or with other large species such as arowana, stingrays, large cats and other large cichlids. An extremely large tank is required to achieve this with any degree of success. Will eat tankmates small enough to be considered food.
One can observe the unique sexual dichromatism of Cichla orinocensis: males look rather like Cichla ocellaris, while females have a colour pattern that reminds one of C. temensis.
The male is larger and develops a nuchal hump as he matures.
All species of Cichla are, as far as it is known, openbrooders and perform bipartental broodcare.
Limited reports of breeding in the hobby.
Cichla: a name used in ancient Greece for a fish that is unknown today. orinocensis: means "originating from the Rio Orinoco".

Due to their large size, Peacock Bass are only really recommended for the experienced fishkeeper that can house them adequately. That said, they are a hardy and robust species that will adapt to a variety of conditions. Peacock Bass are becoming much more available in the hobby and are often seen for sale as cute 5 cm babies, often tempting people into buying a fish they will not be able to care for in the long term. Peacock Bass are also fished as a sport fish.
